Exact Boolean interpolation gives kernel dimensions and S_m-characters of multiplication by L. Semisimplicity yields M_d is permutation representation V_d for d<=m-1 and V_1 thereafter. The projective zero scheme on every coordinate chart is reduced, yielding saturation I=(xi*xj:i<j). Equivariant kernel exact sequence and Young rule then prove each specified multiplicity-one Specht constituent. No induction from small cases is used; exact-arithmetic replay matches predicted ranks and characters.

originality.rationale: The final finding is the equivariant Specht-module decomposition of every layer of the saturation defect, not the scalar Hilbert function. Actual same-object prior Example 3.2 of Dimca–Sticlaru proves the 4-variable Cayley numerical Hilbert series; the 2011 nodal theorem implies much of the all-size dimension function. Those scalar statements do not fix the symmetry characters or imply the asserted multiplicity-free two-row isotypes. A distinct Boolean-interpolation argument and equivariant representation-ring calculation establish the stronger classification. Searches of same-object aliases, nodal syzygy generalizations and the indexed findings did not reveal this representation result. Residual risk remains for an unindexed historical equivariant treatment.

value.rationale: The full variable-permutation symmetry is intrinsic to the elementary symmetric cubic; the finite-length Jacobian saturation quotient represents a genuine embedded defect at the affine cone vertex. The all-size, all-degree multiplicity-free irreducible Specht stratification determines character data invisible to node counts, scalar Hilbert functions or an isolated Cayley cubic example. The theorem identifies which two-row types occur and excludes trivial and standard constituents, a structurally meaningful representation-theoretic invariant. No downstream paper-scale theorem is claimed.
